description: We are a Bishkek team taking on the Earth System Trend Detective challenge. Our goal: an open-source tool that lets anyone check whether a change in NASA Earth data is a real trend or just noise, with honest statistics and a clear web interface. We are looking for a Python developer, a frontend developer, someone strong in statistics or data analysis, and a designer/storyteller for the demo. Working languages: Russian and English.
summary:
TrendeX is a decision-support web app for pasture agencies in Kyrgyzstan. For each 1 km pasture area it combines a relative level with a 2000–2025 NDVI trend tested for statistical reliability, and returns a verdict and next step: recommend, field check first, or not recommended. It uses open NASA data (MODIS, NASADEM, IMERG, GLDAS) and states its limits openly: most areas show no reliable trend, and only the few with a reliable decline go on the first field-check list.
TrendeX turns 25 years of NASA satellite data into one tested answer for every pasture area: how good it is, where it is heading, how far to trust it, and what to do next. Built for Kyrgyzstan's pastures.
details:
TrendeX is a decision-support web app for pasture agencies in Kyrgyzstan. For any ~1 km pasture area in Naryn oblast it gives one plain answer: how good the pasture is relative to other pastures (level), which way it has moved in 2000–2025 (trend, statistically tested), how far that can be trusted, where better options are nearby, and what to do next (recommend, recommend with caveat, field check first, not recommended).

How it works: MODIS NDVI (MOD13A3) summer series, MODIS land cover (MCD12Q1) and NASADEM slope define pasture and level. The trend uses the Theil–Sen slope and the Hamed–Rao Mann–Kendall test with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction across all pasture pixels. A separate, clearly labelled "beyond weather" layer uses an XGBoost model on GPM IMERG, GLDAS, MOD11A2 and MOD10A2 to estimate weather-expected greenness. The level and trend verdicts use no machine learning.

Result: in Naryn, 76% of 44,906 km² of pasture shows no reliable trend, 8.1% is reliably greening and 2.0% (917 km²) is reliably declining. The 2% are the first field-check candidates. We state that NDVI flags few areas and that greening is not automatically better pasture: in Suusamyr, users reported decline while NDVI rose (GIZ, 2019).

Benefit and impact: pasture agencies and committees get a ranked field-check list; herders get better-targeted checks.

Tools: Python 3.11 (NumPy, pandas, SciPy, pymannkendall, rasterio, Shapely, XGBoost) for offline processing; React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Leaflet and Tailwind CSS for the map app; a static site on Cloudflare Pages; data cube and model on Hugging Face.

Limits and next steps: validated only for Naryn; land cover is used for 2020 only. A Central Asia layer exists but is not validated locally and should not be used outside Naryn yet. Next: validate with the Kyrgyz pasture department and field data.

AI use: Claude Code (Anthropic) helped write and debug the data pipeline, statistics, web app and model-training code, and summarise the literature. Claude Design helped lay out the slides. The team chose the data and method and reviewed the code and results.
